summary.text: 难 is the standardized simplified form of 難. The traditional graph is analyzed as a phonosemantic bird-name graph: 隹 marks the bird category, and an element associated with 堇 supplies a sound cue. 難 is also reported as a borrowed spelling for the separate word “difficult”; the bird-name’s pronunciation is unrecovered, so the proposed sound match cannot be confirmed.

formation.text: Traditional 難 is analyzed as a phonosemantic graph for a bird name, with 隹 contributing the bird category and an element associated with 堇 supplying a sound cue. A historical lexicographic account also describes an alternate bird graph written with 鳥 and 堇. These analyses concern 難, not a component breakdown of simplified 难; early graphic history remains contested.

components.text: In 難, 隹 contributes the bird category in the proposed bird-name analysis. Historical accounts also describe a bird graph written with 鳥; the bird’s identity and pronunciation are unresolved.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin readings are 隹 zhuī and 難 nán. This current pair does not establish a historical sound role for 隹.

components.text: The element associated with 堇 in 難 is analyzed as phonetic. Accounts differ over the early graphic history of related forms, including changes to the lower part; the early depiction is disputed.

sound_limitation.text: The reading comparisons do not independently establish that the element in 難 is 堇 or prove its historical phonetic role.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin readings are 堇 jǐn and 難 nán; their current readings do not establish an ancient relationship.
In Baxter–Sagart’s Old Chinese entries, 堇 *[g]rə[r] and 難 *nˤar for “difficult” can be compared. This comparison does not establish that the element in 難 is 堇 or prove its historical phonetic role.

history.text: Reports describe differing structures for 難: some bronze forms combine 黃 and 隹, while a late Warring States example has 隹 and the phonetic element. The available accounts do not give a complete sequence of graphic changes.
The 1935 simplified-character list included 难 as a counterpart of 難; the 1956 scheme standardized 难 as its simplified form. A specific cursive derivation is not established.

uncertainties.text: The bird-name is recorded in historical lexicographic accounts, but its earliest surviving occurrence, identity and pronunciation, and a complete graphic sequence are unresolved. Interpretations of the early 堇-related form also differ.

The proposed reuse of 難 for “difficult” depends on similarity between the spoken bird-name and a separate word. Because the bird-name’s pronunciation is unrecovered, that sound match remains unconfirmed.

senses.text: Historical lexicographic accounts record 難 as a bird name; the earliest surviving occurrence is not dated here.

Bronze contexts are reported for 難 meaning “difficult,” including uses glossed as difficult to do and difficult to approach. The inscriptions are not dated here, so priority among early senses is unresolved.
難 is also used as a noun meaning “difficulty”; the evidence gives no first attestation for this use.

developments.text: The proposed account is that a graph used for a bird name was reused to write the separate word “difficult” because the spoken forms were thought similar. The bird-name’s pronunciation is unrecovered, so this sound match remains unconfirmed.

limitations.text: The dates of the bird-name and difficulty uses are unresolved. 難老 is recorded as a compound glossed “long-lived,” but this does not establish an independent single-character sense or a connection with “difficult.”
